memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Maya chose the Delta itinerary over a comparable American itinerary because the $22 difference bought a more comfortable post-workshop airport-transfer margin; Delta was favored without being treated as exclusive.

messages.content: I need to sort out Philadelphia next. The workshop is Tuesday through Thursday in Center City, starting at 8:30 Tuesday and ending at 4:30 Thursday. I can leave Minneapolis after 3:30 Monday, and airfare needs to stay under $700.
What are the travel dates, and do you want me to limit this to nonstops or include a connection if it improves the timing or fare?
Monday, July 20 through Thursday, July 23. A nonstop is better, but show me a connection if it is meaningfully cheaper. I mostly need a realistic Thursday departure after the workshop.

I found three workable economy combinations. The strongest Monday outbound choices are a Delta nonstop leaving MSP at 5:15 p.m. and reaching PHL at 8:48 p.m., or an American nonstop from 4:40 p.m. to 8:16 p.m. There is also a United itinerary through Chicago from 4:25 p.m. to 9:38 p.m., but the savings are modest and the connection adds risk before an 8:30 start.
Agreed, skip the connection. What does Thursday look like once you account for getting out of the workshop and reaching PHL?

From central Philadelphia, I would allow 35 to 55 minutes by car at that hour, then target arrival at PHL at least 90 minutes before departure. If the workshop ends promptly at 4:30 and your bag is with you, a car around 4:40 makes 5:20 to 5:35 a reasonable airport-arrival range. That makes departures before 7:00 tight. The practical nonstop returns are American at 7:12 p.m., arriving MSP at 9:10 p.m., and Delta at 7:45 p.m., arriving at 9:42 p.m.
I will have my suitcase with me, so no hotel stop. Are both round trips within the allowance?

Yes. Pairing the American flights is $548 round trip: Monday 4:40–8:16 p.m. and Thursday 7:12–9:10 p.m. Pairing Delta is $570: Monday 5:15–8:48 p.m. and Thursday 7:45–9:42 p.m. Both are nonstop standard economy and include a regular carry-on. Checked-bag charges, if any, are separate.
The American return leaves less room than I would like if the last workshop discussion runs over.

That is the main tradeoff. For the 7:12 flight, I would want you in a car no later than 4:50; a 20-minute overrun would start consuming the airport buffer. The 7:45 Delta departure gives about 33 more minutes and still stays $130 below the airfare cap.
Then favor Delta here. The extra $22 is worth the better Thursday margin, assuming there is no schedule catch.

There is no timing catch in the displayed itinerary. Monday’s 5:15 departure clears your 3:30 constraint by 1 hour 45 minutes and gets you to Philadelphia the night before the workshop. Thursday’s 7:45 departure gives you a sensible transfer window after the 4:30 finish. The fare is nonrefundable, with changes allowed subject to fare difference; the displayed cancellation window is 24 hours after purchase.
Before we go any further, give me that one and the best backup in a clean comparison. Do not book either.

Primary: Delta nonstop, $570 round trip. Depart MSP Monday, July 20 at 5:15 p.m.; arrive PHL at 8:48 p.m. Return Thursday, July 23 at 7:45 p.m.; arrive MSP at 9:42 p.m. After the workshop, leave the Center City site around 4:40 p.m.; expected PHL arrival is 5:20–5:35, leaving roughly 2 hours 10 minutes before departure.

Backup: American nonstop, $548 round trip. Depart MSP Monday at 4:40 p.m.; arrive PHL at 8:16 p.m. Return Thursday at 7:12 p.m.; arrive MSP at 9:10 p.m. The same transfer estimate leaves about 1 hour 37 minutes to 1 hour 52 minutes at PHL, so it is workable but less forgiving of an overrun or traffic.

Both are standard economy, both remain under the $700 allowance, and neither has been booked.
